pattern.crimePattern: fraudster recognised by a victim's relative silences her
pattern.notes: Fictional hotel; the overseas-job scam is a common pattern, no real case retold.

ob.text: Hotel owner Amos Kibet reports that his night receptionist, Faith Chepkoech (26), was found dead at the front desk of Mapumziko Hotel, off Haile Selassie Avenue, at 23:58, shortly after a citywide power blackout ended.

people.name: Faith Chepkoech
people.bio: Studied hospitality at night school. Kept a small notebook in the desk drawer for guests' requests.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 20s, short natural hair, white hotel receptionist blouse with a name pin, bright hopeful smile, ID-photo framing

people.name: Paul Njeru
people.bio: Checked in two nights ago. Pays cash. Says he is in Nairobi to interview candidates for jobs in the Gulf.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 40s, shiny grey suit a size too big, gold-coloured watch, practised salesman's smile, ID-photo framing

people.name: Kennedy Ouma
people.bio: Complained loudly to Faith about the hot water at 22:30. Several guests heard him.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 30s, sweat-soaked shirt, loosened tie, furious and exhausted after hours in a stuck lift, ID-photo framing

people.name: Zawadi Mwende
people.bio: Cooks breakfast and late suppers. Borrowed KSh 3,000 from Faith last month and hasn't paid it back.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, late 30s, white cook's apron and headscarf, a paper bag of candles in her hand, frightened eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Amos Kibet
people.bio: Lives in Kileleshwa. Came as soon as the lift technician called.

people.name: Selina Waweru
people.bio: Called out to free a guest stuck in the hotel's old lift.

people.name: Hassan Juma
people.bio: Sells candles, airtime and milk. Open until midnight.

places.name: The hotel lift, stuck between floors 1 and 2

locations.name: Mapumziko Hotel
locations.description: A three-storey budget hotel off Haile Selassie Avenue. Fourteen rooms, one old lift, a narrow concrete staircase, a reception desk with a key board behind it. The scene sketch shows all three floors.

hotspots.label: Front desk
hotspots.text: Faith is slumped behind the desk. The report says she was strangled with the lanyard of her own key ring. Her reception candle is still in the drawer, unlit, with a box of matches.

hotspots.label: Wall clock behind the desk
hotspots.text: An electric clock. Its hands stopped when the power went.

hotspots.label: Guest register
hotspots.text: Rooms, names, nights. Faith's neat handwriting.

hotspots.label: Faith's desk notebook
hotspots.text: A small exercise book for guests' requests. The last page isn't a request.

hotspots.label: The staircase
hotspots.text: In the sketch, each landing lights up as Amani climbs. White candle-wax drips mark the steps.

hotspots.label: 2nd-floor corridor, outside room 12
hotspots.text: On the floor outside room 12: a candle burned down to a stub, stuck to the tiles by its own wax.

hotspots.label: The lift
hotspots.text: The lift doors are open now. Taped inside: the technician's call-out sheet.

image.brief: the reception desk of a cheap Nairobi city-centre hotel lit only by a single candle, a wooden key board with numbered hooks behind, a dark staircase rising on the right, deep shadows, no people

body.note: Report language only; no image of the body.

image.brief: a cheap round electric wall clock stopped at ten past eleven, photographed by torchlight against a cream wall

body.keyboard: Key board: room 7 key on its hook. Room 12 key NOT on its hook.

body.text:
Rm 7 hot water!! — told Amos.

The man in 12 is the agent who took Mama's 180,000 for the Qatar job. He called himself Peter Ndungu then. Police tomorrow first thing.

body.label: White wax drips from the desk, up the stairs, to the 2nd-floor landing. None on the 1st-floor corridor.
White candle, burned to 2 cm, stuck to the tiles outside room 12.

image.brief: a white household candle burned down to a two-centimetre stub, stuck by its own wax to green floor tiles beside a hotel room door numbered 12

facts.text: Faith Chepkoech was found dead at the front desk of Mapumziko Hotel at 23:58.
A citywide blackout hit at 23:10. Power came back at 23:55.
Faith was strangled with the lanyard of her own key ring after a struggle at the desk.
Faith's reception candle was still in the drawer, unlit, with the matches.
The electric clock behind the desk stopped at 23:10, when the power went.
Register: room 12, P. Njeru, three nights, paid cash.
Register: room 7, K. Ouma, one night. Rooms 3 and 9 empty.
Room 12's key isn't on the key board. Guests hand it in when they go out, so its guest was in the hotel all night.
Faith's note: the man in 12 is the 'agent' who took her mother's KSh 180,000 for a fake job. Police tomorrow.
White wax drips run from the desk up the stairs to the 2nd floor. None on the 1st-floor corridor.
A burned-down candle stub is stuck to the floor outside the door of room 12.
Lift call-out: stuck 23:10 between floors 1 and 2 with the room-7 guest inside; freed 23:58.
Technician Selina Waweru arrived through the front door at 23:40, coming from a call-out in Ngara.
Zawadi: when the power went, Faith sent her across the road for candles at about 23:11. Faith was alive at the desk.
Kiosk owner: Zawadi bought four candles at about 23:12 and waited twenty minutes for change.
Zawadi's four candles are still wrapped in their paper in her bag.
Amos was at home in Kileleshwa until Selina phoned him at 23:58.
Amos: the cook, Zawadi Mwende, stays late on Thursdays for the suppers. She owes Faith money.
Paul: "I was asleep in my room. I sleep early. I didn't even know there was a blackout."
Paul: "I've never met that girl before this week."
Kennedy: "I spent fifty minutes in a box between floors. Ask the technician."
Kennedy shouted at Faith about the hot water at 22:30 and went up to bed.

interrogations.intro: Amos stands in the doorway of his own hotel as if he's afraid to come in. "She was saving for her diploma. Every shilling."

topics.reply: Njeru in 12? Pays cash every morning. Says he recruits for jobs in Qatar. He asked Faith which school she went to.
Room 7 shouted about hot water all evening. Then he got stuck in my lift. He'll want a refund.
Zawadi is the cook. She stays late Thursdays. She borrowed from Faith; everyone borrows from everyone here.

interrogations.intro: Zawadi still has the paper bag of candles in her hand. "I went for candles. I went for candles and when I came back…"

topics.reply: She said, 'Zawadi, run across, get candles, ours is the last one.' She laughed about it. That was eleven, ten past eleven.
Ask Hassan. The whole street was at his kiosk for candles and he had no coins for change.

interrogations.intro: Paul opens the door of room 12 in a hotel dressing gown, smiling. "Officer. Terrible thing. Terrible."

topics.reply: Somebody left a candle by my door? People are careless in the dark.
Peter Ndungu? I don't know any Peter Ndungu. Njeru, Paul. You have my ID.

interrogations.intro: Kennedy sits on the bottom stair, shirt soaked. "Fifty minutes. Fifty minutes in that coffin."

topics.reply: Yes, I shouted at her about the water. I'm not proud of it. She said sorry like it was her fault.

interrogations.intro: Selina packs her tools. "I came in the front door at twenty to midnight. The desk was dark. I thought the girl had gone upstairs."

topics.reply: He was in that lift the whole time, believe me. He told me about it, loudly.

prosecutor.pass: The killer brought light, and the light went to his own door. That will hold.
fail: This doesn't hold up. In a blackout, someone needed light. Follow it.
No. Who could actually move around that hotel between ten past and half past eleven?

proof.concludes: Faith died during the blackout, after 23:11, in the dark, and her own candle was never lit: the killer brought light.
The light went from the desk up to room 12, whose guest, Paul Njeru, was in the hotel all night.

eliminations.why: Kennedy was stuck in the lift from 23:10 to 23:58.
Zawadi was across the road at the kiosk from 23:11 to about 23:35, and her candles are still wrapped.
Amos was at home in Kileleshwa until he was phoned at 23:58.
Selina was on a call-out in Ngara and only arrived through the front door at 23:40.

reconstruction.text: Two years ago, a man calling himself Peter Ndungu takes KSh 180,000 from Faith's mother for a job in Qatar that doesn't exist.
Wednesday. 'Paul Njeru' checks into room 12 and pays cash. On Thursday evening Faith recognises his voice and writes it down: police tomorrow.
23:10. Stima imepotea. The lift stops with a guest inside. Faith sends Zawadi across the road for candles.
Paul comes down the stairs with a candle from his room. At the dark desk he kills her with the lanyard of her own keys.
He climbs back to the 2nd floor, wax dripping, and sets the candle down outside his door while he finds his key in the dark. It burns down there.

tier1.line: In a blackout everyone needs light. Faith's candle was never lit. So whose candle was it?

tier2.line: Wax from the desk to the 2nd floor, and a stub outside one door. Check the register for that door.

glossary.def: Mother; also a respectful way to address an older woman.

ui.beatNotes: The scene is a police floor-plan sketch of all three floors. Tapping the stairs reveals the wax trail floor by floor. First case where following evidence across space matters.
